children: South Korea's core inflation could slow in the coming months partly due to the won's appreciation, Barclays's Bum Ki Son says. The economist expects the Korean currency's recent strength against the dollar to ease pressure on tradable-goods prices, citing the won's 13% gain over the past two months. He estimates that a 10% appreciation of the won typically leads to a decline in core-goods inflation, mostly driven by tradable goods, over the following six to 10 months. He expects the recent sharp increase in core-goods inflation to slow. The country earlier Wednesday reported that core inflation accelerated to 3.4% in August from 2.6% in July. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
